subtitle: Understanding common song structures and their theoretical foundations

introduction.title: Song Forms: The Architecture of Music
introduction.text: Song form is the large-scale organization of musical material that creates coherent structures listeners can follow and remember. These forms represent time-tested solutions to the challenge of balancing repetition (for familiarity) with contrast (for interest). Understanding form helps us analyze how songs create their emotional journeys and structural logic.

columns.title: Structural Templates
columns.text: Time-tested patterns for organizing musical material

columns.title: Unity vs. Variety
columns.text: Balance repetition for familiarity with contrast for interest

columns.title: Listener Guidance
columns.text: Predictable patterns help listeners follow musical narratives

cards.title: AABA (32-bar Song Form)
cards.description: Classic American popular song form with contrasting bridge

fields.label: Theory
fields.value: A sections establish main theme, B section provides harmonic and melodic contrast

fields.label: Harmonic Approach
fields.value: A: tonic-centered, B: modulation or relative keys

cards.title: Verse-Chorus Form
cards.description: Modern popular song form with alternating verse and chorus

fields.label: Structure
fields.value: V - C - V - C - B - C

fields.label: Theory
fields.value: Verses develop narrative, choruses provide emotional/harmonic climax

fields.label: Harmonic Approach
fields.value: Verses: stable progressions, Choruses: climactic harmony

cards.title: Binary Form (AB)
cards.description: Two contrasting sections, each typically repeated

fields.label: Theory
fields.value: A section establishes key, B section provides contrast and return

fields.label: Harmonic Approach
fields.value: A: tonic to dominant, B: explores related keys, returns to tonic

cards.title: Ternary Form (ABA)
cards.description: Three-part form with return to opening material

fields.label: Theory
fields.value: A establishes main theme, B contrasts, A returns (often varied)

fields.label: Harmonic Approach
fields.value: A: home key, B: contrasting key, A: return to home key

cards.title: Twelve-Bar Blues Form
cards.description: Foundational blues structure with set harmonic progression

fields.label: Harmonic Approach
fields.value: Built on I-IV-V relationships with blues-specific extensions

cards.title: Through-Composed
cards.description: Continuously developing form without exact repetition

fields.label: Theory
fields.value: Each section introduces new material, constant development

fields.label: Harmonic Approach
fields.value: Continuously modulating or developing harmonic language

fields.label: Key Questions
fields.value: How do sections contrast? What creates unity? How does each section serve the overall form?

fields.label: Key Questions
fields.value: What is the tonal plan? How do key relationships create structure? Where do modulations occur?

fields.label: Key Questions
fields.value: How are phrases organized within sections? What phrase lengths are used? How do phrases relate?

fields.label: Key Questions
fields.value: What musical ideas unify the form? How are motifs developed? What provides melodic coherence?

cards.title: Pre-Chorus Addition
cards.description: Builds energy and expectation before choruses

fields.label: Modern
fields.value: V - PC - C - V - PC - C

fields.label: Common In
fields.value: Contemporary pop, rock, when additional build is needed

cards.title: Multiple Bridges
cards.description: Provides multiple contrast points and development

fields.label: Traditional
fields.value: V - C - V - C - B - C

fields.label: Modern
fields.value: V - C - V - C - B1 - C - B2 - C

fields.label: Common In
fields.value: Progressive rock, complex pop songs, extended forms

cards.title: Extended Outros
cards.description: Allows for gradual fade or extended development

fields.label: Modern
fields.value: V - C - V - C - C - C (fade/extend)

cards.title: Repetition & Return
items: Repetition gives listeners musical anchors and creates the satisfaction of return to familiar material.

cards.title: Contrast & Development
items: Contrast provides variety and emotional development, keeping listeners engaged throughout the song.

cards.title: Proportion & Balance
items: Well-proportioned sections create a sense of architectural balance and structural inevitability.

cards.title: Goal-Direction
items: Good forms create expectation and direct listener attention toward important structural moments.

cards.title: Step-by-Step Process
items: 1. Listen for section changes and repetitions
2. Map the sections using letters (A, B, C)

cards.title: What to Listen For
items: Melodic returns: Same or similar melodies
Rhythmic changes: Different feels or grooves
Lyrical patterns: Verse vs. chorus content
